gaps.sentence: I'd rather ___ by card than carry cash.
gaps.explanation: pay by card/in cash is the fixed pattern for the method of payment.

gaps.sentence: The storm ___ a lot of damage to the roof.
gaps.explanation: do damage to something is the collocation; past tense 'did' is needed here.

gaps.sentence: Unlike some politicians, she ___ her promises.
gaps.hint: collocation with 'promises' (she is unlike other politicians)
gaps.explanation: keep a promise means to do what you promised; the contrast with other politicians shows the positive verb.

gaps.sentence: She ___ very well in her end-of-year exams.
gaps.hint: collocation: to ___ well in an exam
gaps.explanation: do well in an exam is the standard phrase meaning to perform successfully.

gaps.sentence: The referee warned the players not to ___ the rules.
gaps.hint: collocation with 'rules' (the referee warns against it)
gaps.explanation: break the rules means to disobey them; the context ('warned not to') requires this meaning.

gaps.sentence: The crash left several passengers seriously ___.
gaps.explanation: seriously injured is the standard collocation describing bad injuries in accidents.

gaps.sentence: A true friend will always ___ a secret.
gaps.explanation: keep a secret is the fixed collocation for not telling it to anyone.

gaps.sentence: We should ___ an effort to arrive on time.
gaps.explanation: make an effort is the fixed collocation meaning to try hard.
